edges.description: Systemic macrophage activation constitutes the HLH syndrome.
Hemophagocytic activity in bone marrow is a defining HLH finding.
Fever is a cardinal feature of HLH and HLH-like systemic illness.
Thrombocytopenia occurs in a minority of the paediatric series.
Hypofibrinogenemia is part of the HLH laboratory picture.
Anemia is the commonest cytopenia in the paediatric series.
Neutropenia occurs in half of the paediatric series.
Hyperferritinemia is the most frequent laboratory abnormality of HLH in this disease.
Hypertriglyceridemia is part of the HLH laboratory picture.
The infiltrate presents clinically as subcutaneous nodules and plaques.

nodes.description: Cytotoxic CD8-positive alpha-beta T cells infiltrate the subcutaneous fat lobule and rim individual adipocytes, producing lobular panniculitis and, when clonal, SPTCL. Tumor cells in carriers acquire additional somatic mutations in epigenetic-regulation and signal-transduction genes. Lymphoma can recur as clonally unrelated episodes in the same patient, and the spectrum extends to other T-cell lymphomas in a few carriers; some paediatric biopsies show panniculitis without sufficient evidence of lymphoma, which is why the neoplastic nature of the lesion is debated.
